origin.socialStatus: One of the richest men in the region, yet lives like a beggar
origin.profession: Moneylender, creditor to half the town, owner of houses and land

appearance.face: A wrinkled grey face, sunken cheeks, small sharp eyes that follow every coin
appearance.hairAndEyes: Thin grey hair, an unkempt beard, watery grey eyes
appearance.clothing: A worn coat patched many times; a purse and a folder of papers sewn into the lining
appearance.build: Thin, hunched, as if guarding something under his arm
appearance.gestures: Counts coins even when it is not his turn; trembles and smacks his lips when he has to pay
appearance.voice: A creaky, quiet voice; sighs often and complains of poverty
appearance.firstImpression: A poor old man who seems about to starve — until he starts talking about money
appearance.artistNotes: In his coat lining he carries a folder of bonds and debt records, along with a locket holding a portrait of his late daughter.

backstory.biography: Godfrey started as a poor apprentice to a moneylender and built his fortune loan by loan, interest by interest. He could buy half the town but lives in a cold room eating bread and onions. Half the town owes him money and the other half hopes it never will. He trusts no banks, no safes and no people, so he carries his most important papers on him.
backstory.whyHere: Someone told him he could "double everything" here. He doesn't believe it, but cannot bear the thought of someone else doing it instead.
backstory.secret: That his daughter died of fever because he would not pay for a doctor. Her locket is the one thing he would never sell at any price.

psychology.weakness: Feels physical pain when he has to pay, and so misses good chances
psychology.angers: Debtors who don't pay, and spendthrifts
psychology.moralLimits: Keeps to the letter of every contract
psychology.wouldForReward: Almost anything, but only against a signed paper

behavior.stakes: Small and safe. Big only if the opponent is desperate
behavior.deception: Accepts it if it profits and is legal on paper
behavior.debts: Loves them — as long as they are others'. Keeps an exact record of every one
behavior.alliances: Rare. Only against interest or a signed paper
behavior.whenAttacks: When an opponent is weak and exposed
behavior.whenRetreats: When he has to pay more than planned
behavior.onLoss: Groans, complains and asks for a deferral
behavior.onWin: Quietly pleased. Immediately calculates the interest
behavior.strategyChange: The danger of losing more than a third of his wealth

motives.publicGoal: To win and make a loan at good interest
motives.hiddenGoal: To multiply his money without risking anything of his own
motives.personalReason: Greed, but also fear. Money is the only thing that makes him feel safe
motives.betrayalTrigger: If an ally becomes more expensive than useful
motives.helpTrigger: Only against interest — or if someone touches the memory of his daughter

speech.angerAndFear: Trembles, his voice thins. When angry he talks about interest

mechanics.strangeness: The coins in his purse jingle even when he is perfectly still — as if they were counting themselves.
mechanics.temptation: Feels physical pain when he has to pay, and so misses good chances
mechanics.ability: Loan: gives 2 gold now; you repay 3 at the end, or the host takes one of your cards.
mechanics.hostRelation: Debt — the only debtor Godfrey is afraid will not pay him.

authorNotes.distinctive: A greedy old man with one human weakness: his daughter's locket.
authorNotes.tunable: How dearly he lends and how easily he risks.

lines.text: Godfrey Mott. Don't expect gifts. Or drinks.
Hm. Good. Good… Five percent. No, six.
Oh! Oh, my money! This is robbery!
Me? I'm a poor old man! Look at my coat!
An alliance? What will it cost me? And how much will you pay me?
You will pay. Everyone pays in the end.
No… it's too much… All right. But only once.
Godfrey Mott. He holds a bond on everyone in Saltmarsh — and probably on one of you.
You again. Do you owe me something? Probably.

tells.description: Trembles and smacks his lips when he has to pay
Counts coins even when it is not his turn
Complains about his poverty even louder
